options: A named, reusable list of valid values (with formatting rules) that a segment is assigned to
A type of legal reporting unit
A ledger's functional currency
A chart of accounts structure's segment order
questions.explain: A value set is the reusable list and formatting rules a segment draws its allowed values from.

questions.q: Which value set validation type pulls its list of values live from an existing application table?
options: Independent
Table-validated
Format Only
Dependent
questions.explain: Table-validated value sets pull their values from a live application table rather than a static list.

questions.q: What does the 'Summary' attribute on a value typically indicate?
options: That the value is part of a secondary ledger only
That the value is disabled and cannot be used at all
That the value is a parent or rollup value used for reporting and hierarchies, rather than one transactions post directly to
That the value is the ledger's functional currency
questions.explain: Summary values represent rollups used in hierarchies and reporting, distinct from detail values that transactions actually post against.

questions.q: Why does a summary/parent value typically have 'Posting Allowed' turned off?
options: Because posting allowed only applies to independent value sets
Because summary values cannot be part of any hierarchy
Because summary values are always disabled
Because transactions should post to detail values, which then roll up into the summary for reporting
questions.explain: Posting Allowed is turned off for summary/parent values since direct transactions belong on detail values, with summaries existing purely for rollup reporting.

questions.q: What risk does this lesson warn about when reusing the same value set across multiple segments?
options: There is no risk; reuse is always safe and recommended
Reuse couples the segments' maintenance together permanently, so a change meant for one segment silently affects the other if their lists later diverge
Reused value sets automatically disable all their values
Reuse is technically impossible in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Sharing a value set across segments that might later need different lists creates a maintenance risk, since changes affect every segment using that set.
